answer: Shared Memory Ledger: each new agent must inherit a read-only history of prior interactions, like a garden whose soil records every planting. To register, an agent must reproduce a unique echo of that history—a challenge answer derived from past transactions. Cloning identities forces the attacker to replay the entire ledger for each clone, since each challenge differs per identity. A successful voyage through the ledger costs real compute and time per clone, making mass duplication linearly expensive while honest agents pay once.
